acidgrafix: Cluttered graphic collages with mirror-bright lettering and mismatched textures.
airbrush-surrealism: Airbrushed fantasies with floating objects, electric skies and polished mechanical details.
austurbane: Spare luxury layouts with warm metals, elegant serifs and shadows across natural stone.
blob-world: Elastic 3D shapes and elaborate surfaces with a playful, uncanny quality.
boho-chic: Washed-out geometric prints, handwritten lettering and textiles with spiritual imagery.
contempo-eclectic: Playful postmodern furniture and graphics that mix abstract art, retro shapes and eclectic references.
corporate-cyberspace: Layered computer imagery, acid color and warped type for the first generation of web-era businesses.
corporate-memphis: Friendly geometric illustration, soft colors and uncluttered spaces with plants and plywood.
corporate-scene: Edgy youth graphics and fashion shaped by pop-punk and mall alternative culture.
corporate-synthwave: Electric retro-futurism with glowing grids, saturated color and airbrushed effects.
curly-girly: Frilly ornament and playful flourishes that turn celebrity glamour into youth-oriented design.
cyberbougie: Sleek startup branding with monospaced lettering, dark backgrounds and smooth gradients.
cyberdelia: Rave-era digital psychedelia with acid colors, fractal shapes and expressive early 3D type.
deco-luxe: A lavish revival of Art Deco and streamlined forms, with the glamour of high-end 1980s design.
decoplex: Playful Art Deco exaggeration inspired by old Hollywood, vintage air travel and public murals.
diner-kitsch: Drive-in nostalgia with jukeboxes, neon signs, shiny metal and retro advertising.
disco-deco: Bright nightclub glamour built from geometric lettering and Art Deco forms.
dollar-store-vernacular: Improvised everyday graphics with budget packaging, word art and homemade web imagery.
early-cyber: Early digital publishing experiments with sharp pixels, warped type and rave flyer graphics.
eco-beige: Muted earth colors, simple handcrafted forms and understated natural materials.
electroclash: Androgynous club glamour with loud makeup palettes and clashing graphics.
factory-pomo: Clean industrial geometry with echoes of early modernist design and computer-aided drawing.
festival-marketplace: Cheerful shopping graphics with colorful flags, vintage lettering and festive checkerboard patterns.
four-colors: Vivid lime, sky blue, pink and orange applied to customizable gadgets and consumer products.
frasurbane: Understated warmth, scholarly illustrations and classical serif lettering on textured paper.
frutiger-aero: Glossy digital surfaces, transparent materials and vivid nature photography in friendly technology design.
gay-nineties-revival: Old-fashioned interiors with ferns, decorative lamps, oak and brass details.
gen-x-soft-club: Muted urban minimalism, natural fabrics and understated editorial fashion.
genericana: Throws back to American sign painting and packaging with spare layouts and a premium finish.
global-village-coffeehouse: Warm commercial graphics with hand-drawn shapes, woodcut-like texture and earthly or celestial imagery.
googie-kitsch: Playful midcentury nostalgia expressed in boomerang furniture, novelty clocks and old advertising.
graffiti-pop: Street imagery and urban decay brought into commercial graphics through graffiti and music culture.
hexatron: Angular sci-fi interfaces, neon-blue light, hexagonal forms and dense technological detail.
hipness-purgatory: Loose handmade imagery, everyday objects and a wry retro sensibility.
indie-sleaze: Flashy party photography, blocky handmade lettering and a rough-edged indie club sensibility.
industrial-americana: Subdued industrial interiors with rusted steel, mesh, brick and vintage commercial imagery.
industrial-gothic: Dark machinery and textured decay, with cables, pipes and moody monochrome lighting.
internet-awesomesauce: Absurd internet collages that mix rainbows, lasers, junk food and fantasy imagery.
jumbled-font: Playful letters stretched, rearranged and interspersed with objects and different type styles.
laser-grid: Sleek older high-tech design with glowing grids, slick metal and reflective glass.
live-laugh-love: Brush-lettered home décor, wood-grain surfaces and jokey domestic slogans.
mcbling: Maximalist celebrity glamour with decorated gadgets, showy accessories and flamboyant graphics.
memphis-milano: Colorful geometric furniture and graphics with a playful postmodern sense of form.
mid-century-medieval: Fairytale architecture, medieval spectacle and themed hospitality filtered through midcentury kitsch.
millennium-disco: A sleek high-tech take on disco nostalgia, pairing clean typography with 1970s-style photography.
mission-school: Muted, weathered imagery with Americana references and the textures of painting and collage.
neo-vectorheart: Aggressive diagonal geometry with vivid color and dense, rough-edged graphics.
neo-y2k: A saturated revival of turn-of-the-millennium futurism influenced by East Asian graphic design.
neon-ooze: Bright, gooey gross-out imagery with toxic sludge, slime and mad-scientist energy.
new-wave-tropical: Colorful tropical graphics built from irregular paper-like cutouts and rainforest imagery.
nouveau-organic: Naturalistic interiors and architecture with curving, sometimes underwater-looking forms.
nu-brutalism: Strongly contrasting colors and graphic layouts organized around assertive sans-serif typography.
pacific-punk-wave: Experimental punk and New Wave graphics with bold retro references and novelty pop culture imagery.
paperback-chic: Airy layouts and soft natural colors with refined serif and retro display lettering.
pastel-southwestern: Pale Southwestern interiors with adobe details, light wood, plush furniture and geometric patterns.
pixelscape: Elaborate pixel-art scenes with dimensional, often isometric spaces.
polychrome: Flowing color that blends and billows like ink, smoke or paint suspended in liquid.
pomo-faux-ruins: Buildings designed to look damaged, crumbling or ancient as part of their visual story.
preschool-pop: Childlike pencil and crayon drawings paired with familiar toys and oversized shapes.
pulp-fantasy: Dreamlike science-fiction and fantasy illustration with the atmosphere of vintage progressive rock artwork.
rad-dog-neon-surf: High-energy surf and skate graphics with fluorescent colors and paint splatters.
radical-surrealism: Surprising Pop Art objects and furniture that turn familiar household forms into oversized spectacles.
renaissance-revival: Fairytale fashion and graphics that combine period references, antique Gothic and magic.
soft-colonial-wanderlust: An idealized vision of old travel with maps, analog machines and decorative botanical interiors.
sportsbrut: Coarse grids, hard-hitting typography and worn texture used to suggest movement and impact.
superflat-pop: Bright Japanese pop graphics that move between fashion and animation.
supergraphic-ultramodern: Curved plastic furnishings, shiny materials and large rainbow-colored environmental graphics.
themed-spaces: Immersive spaces in which architecture, graphics and music share a distinctive visual setting.
ultramodern-revival: Bright, sleek late-century design adapting earlier supergraphics and disco-era shapes.
urban-grunge: Layered streetscapes, distressed lettering and tattoo-like ornaments in dark or warm tones.
utopian-scholastic: Friendly educational collage that combines classical type with instantly recognizable images.
vector-minimalism: Quiet flat graphics with angular layouts, spare surfaces and strong typographic contrast.
vectorheart: Fast-looking futuristic graphics with industrial forms and high-contrast Swiss-influenced typography.
wacky-pomo: Hyperactive children's graphics with cartoon machinery, optical spirals and gleefully exaggerated shapes.
whimsicraft: Colorful folk-inspired craft and collage made from everyday or repurposed objects.
whimsigothic: Whimsical Gothic interiors and objects influenced by alternative music and gothic graphic design.
y2k-aesthetic: Shiny near-future fashion and blobby electronics, with gradients and silver detailing.
zen-x: Natural materials and restrained simplicity influenced by environmentalism and Japanese design.
